items.headline: [Podcast] From Protocol to Patient: Inside Clinical Supply with Almac Clinical Services
items.preview: This podcast series explores the complexities of clinical trial supply chains.
items.article:
Biopharma companies bringing scientific breakthroughs out of the lab and into the real world do so while navigating a complex global supply chain. Before a single patient is enrolled, before the first site is opened, an enormous amount of planning happens to ensure investigational medicines reach patients safely, reliably, and on time.
This six-part podcast series follows the journey of clinical trial supplies from the earliest planning stages all the way through packaging, distribution, and global regulatory release.
Why this matters: Understanding the logistics and strategies involved in clinical supply can significantly impact trial success and patient safety.

items.headline: AB Science cuts three trials in pipeline reset
items.preview: AB Science discontinues three trials to focus on ALS and AML programs.
items.article:
French biotech AB Science is discontinuing three masitinib trials as it concentrates its clinical resources on an ALS phase 3 programme and the early-stage development of AB8939 in acute myeloid leukaemia.
The move turns a temporary suspension announced in April into a broader pipeline reset, following questions from European regulators about whether AB Science had sufficient resources and organisational structure to conduct its trials.
Why this matters: This strategic shift aims to streamline operations and focus on programs with the potential for significant impact, despite the challenges posed by limited resources.

items.headline: Esophagectomy shows feasible short-term outcomes in octogenarian esophageal cancer patients
items.preview: A study shows that esophagectomy can be safely performed in elderly patients.
items.article:
Esophageal cancer, a formidable malignancy with generally poor prognosis, has traditionally posed significant treatment challenges, particularly in elderly patients. A recent study published in BMC Geriatrics challenges this cautious approach, providing compelling evidence supporting the feasibility and relative safety of curative esophagectomy in patients aged 80 and above.
The study emphasizes the importance of comprehensive preoperative assessment and highlights advancements in minimally invasive surgical techniques that improve perioperative safety.
Why this matters: This research opens doors for more elderly patients to access potentially life-saving treatment, reshaping surgical oncology paradigms.

items.headline: STAT+: A breakthrough in pancreatic cancer has experts excited — and braced for what’s to come
items.preview: A new pancreatic cancer drug has generated significant excitement among experts.
items.article:
When researchers started planning a pancreatic cancer conference, the aim was to offer a counterpart to a regular U.S. meeting. Then came the biggest shake-up in pancreatic cancer care in decades. Experts likened the recent clinical trial performance of a new drug to other milestones in cancer treatment.
Why this matters: This breakthrough could potentially change the landscape of pancreatic cancer treatment, prompting discussions on future implications and challenges.

items.headline: Top Companies Pledge Nature Goals but Fail to Ensure Accountability
items.preview: A study reveals major corporations' biodiversity promises lack transparency.
items.article:
A groundbreaking new study published in One Earth reveals a stark disconnect between corporate biodiversity pledges and the ability to hold companies accountable for their environmental impact. Researchers found that while 79% of major corporations claim to have biodiversity commitments, only 13% articulate these commitments clearly enough for external evaluation.
Why this matters: Establishing clear frameworks for accountability is essential for tracking genuine progress in biodiversity conservation and ensuring that corporate actions align with environmental stewardship.
